description: Spring reverb, a convolution of a real spring tank, with two inputs driving the tank and both a wet and a mixed output

params.text: Crossfades the MIX output between the dry signal at IN 1 and the reverb
Sets how hard that input drives the spring tank, marked from -12dBu to 14dBu
Sets the high-pass filter on the signal going into the tank, from 200Hz to 4000Hz

inputs.text: Scales the drive of the input on that side, 0-10V spanning nothing to the full drive its slider sets; with nothing patched the drive is whatever the slider says
An audio input into the spring tank, and the only signal fed to the dry side of the MIX output
An audio input into the spring tank, which never reaches the dry side of the MIX output
Shifts the dry and wet balance at the MIX output; the voltage is divided by 10 and added to the balance knob

outputs.text: The dry signal at IN 1 crossfaded with the reverb, clamped to -10V to 10V
The reverb on its own with no dry signal, clamped to -10V to 10V

notes: both input level sliders come up fully down, so nothing reaches the spring tank and the WET output stays silent until one of them is raised.
